steps.action: Confirm the house is titled in the trust and that the trust is revocable (included in the gross estate) so the date-of-death step-up applies.
steps.basis: IRC §1014 via IRS FAQ; Rev. Rul. 2023-2

steps.action: Keep the house as the parent's principal residence with the homeowners' exemption on file — Prop 19 only covers a 'family home' eligible for the exemption through the transferor's ownership and occupation.

Use annual-exclusion gifts of cash ($19,000 per recipient in 2026; $20,000 in 2027) to reduce a taxable estate. Avoid gifting the house itself: gifted property does not receive the date-of-death basis.
Trust becomes irrevocable. Serve the statutory notification by trustee on every beneficiary and heir.
Obtain an EIN for the estate/trust (free on IRS.gov) for bank accounts and income tax filings.
Obtain a date-of-death fair-market-value appraisal of each property — it sets the heir's stepped-up basis and the Prop 19 market-value test.
Trust-contest window closes 120 days after notice is served (or 60 days after a requested copy of the trust is delivered, if later).

File a change in ownership statement (death of real property owner) with the assessor/recorder in each county where the decedent owned real property. Late filing after the assessor's written request is penalised (greater of $100 or 10% of new-base taxes, capped).
DECISION POINT — to keep part of the parent's low taxable value, move in and make the house the heir's principal residence, and file the homeowners' exemption, both within one year.

steps.when: Within 3 years, or before a sale to a third party
steps.action: File the Prop 19 parent-child exclusion claim with the county assessor.
File Form 706 if the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts exceeds the year-of-death filing threshold, or to elect portability for a surviving spouse; pay any estate tax.

steps.when: 30 days after the Form 706 due date
steps.action: If Form 706 is required, report estate-tax values to the IRS and beneficiaries (consistent basis reporting).
Record a trustee's deed distributing the house to the heir. No documentary transfer tax applies to a transfer by reason of death.
File the decedent's final Form 1040 and the trust/estate's Form 1041 for income earned during administration (e.g., rent).
Report the sale on Schedule D / Form 8949 using the stepped-up basis; gain over basis is taxable (federal rates per Topic 409; CA taxes it as income).

prop19_example.label: Hypothetical round numbers — NOT the owner's property
prop19_example.rule: R&TC §63.2(d): if market value >= taxable value + exclusion, new taxable value = taxable value + (market value - taxable value - exclusion)
